title_as_printed: Results of steady-state solution measurements with O2 at 298.15 K: pg is pressure of gas; (dV/dt) is the gas flow rate; epsilon is the electrical calibration factor; E is the calorimeter voltage output under steady-state conditions. Water flow rate is 2.7 x 10^-8 m3 s-1. Uncertainty given at twice the uncertainty of the means.
pressure_note: Table header: 'pg is pressure of gas'; text (eq. 5): pw and pg are the water vapor and gas pressures, so pg is the gas partial pressure in the bubble. System pressure = atmospheric (mercury barometer) + water head on the bubble (water manometer).

value.what: enthalpy of solution of O2 in water (printed as -dH_sol, so value = -printed), computed by authors from E, epsilon, dV/dt, pg, pw, virial coefficients and dH_cond

value2.what: raw calorimeter voltage output at steady state

uncertainty2.what: twice the uncertainty of the mean (per table title), printed in parentheses after E; split into own column

composition.other_species: pure water (deaerated), no salt; water flow rate 2.7e-8 m3/s

skip_rows.reason: Mean row: 12.031 +- 0.036 kJ/mol (authors' summary of the 36 trials)

notes: The mean dH_sol is -12.031 kJ/mol; uncertainty printed as 'twice the uncertainty of the means' / 'twice the standard deviation of the mean of 0.036 kJ/mol'. The calorimeter measures enthalpy per mole of gas dissolved in flowing water at very low gas mole fraction, so this is effectively the infinite-dilution enthalpy of solution (not stated by this wording; the paper compares with Benson-Krause dH_sol = -12.02 kJ/mol). volume_basis not applicable (no per-volume quantity).
